sections.title: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.narrative: The Bajío corridor (Guanajuato–Querétaro–Aguascalientes) remains the premier nearshoring destination for mid-to-high-value manufacturing, but faces **acute energy-infrastructure constraints** that will define tenant viability over your 36-month horizon. We assess a **60% probability (Sherman Kent: 5/6)** that at least one sub-corridor will experience a material power disruption event (>4 hours unplanned CFE outage) in the next 12 months. Water security is the second-order risk, with **Aguascalientes at highest vulnerability** (Kent: 4/6). Cartel-related extortion is a **manageable but recurring five-figure annual cost** for industrial tenants, concentrated in Guanajuato’s León-Silao sub-corridor. action_lines.action: Do not acquire in León-Silao without a dedicated on-site security contract (mid-six-figure annual cost). Prefer Irapuato or Celaya for lower extortion incidence.
Querétaro is the lowest-risk sub-corridor for security, but water access must be contractually guaranteed in lease agreements. Prefer El Marqués industrial parks with private water treatment plants.

Aguascalientes requires a water-rights audit before acquisition. Expect tenants to demand backup water storage (mid-six-figure capital cost per 100,000 sq ft). Do not proceed without a CFE reliability letter of intent for the specific substation.
Execute >9% and >51% positions immediately. Monitor Kalshi volume for >18% contract – if volume exceeds $5,000, add $25,000 notional.
